headline: The app now writes one short log line per visit to its web addresses, leaving out personal data. It is safe to ship.
what_changed: Each time the app answers a web address, it now records one line: the kind of request, which web address, whether it worked, and how long it took.
This makes it easier to see which calls fail and which are slow, for example when someone submits a loan application.

The new line deliberately leaves out the form contents, the extra information sent with each request, and anything after a '?' in the web address. So SSNs, bank details and login details are not recorded.
These lines go to the same outside log service the app already uses (Better Stack / Logtail, which keeps logs for 30 days).

risks.title: Requests that crash are not logged
risks.explanation: The new line is only written after the app has finished answering. If a request crashes with an unexpected error, that request gets no log line. So the most serious failures can be missing from this new view. Your error monitoring may still catch them, but a developer could easily add a log line for crashes too.

risks.title: More log lines sent to the paid log service
risks.explanation: Every request now sends one extra line to the outside log service, so log volume grows with traffic. Each line is tiny and is sent in the background, so customers won't see any slowdown. If your log plan charges by volume, keep an eye on the bill.

questions_for_developer: Can we also log a line when a request crashes with an unexpected error, so the worst failures show up in the same place?
Will any future web address include personal details in the address itself (for example a customer ID or email)? The new log records the full address, minus anything after a '?'.
good_news: The developer kept personal data out on purpose. Today the loan application address contains no personal details, so nothing sensitive ends up in the outside log service.
The change is small and self-contained, and it doesn't change how loan applications are handled.
Logs are sent in the background, so this won't slow down pages for customers.
